full_judgment:
3. Case of the preemptors, in short, was that one Tabarakullah was owner in possession in 2.10 acres of land to the extent of 14 annas interest while his mother Ayesha Khatun was owner in possession in the rest 2 annas of Khatian No. 199 After death of said Ayesha Khatun, Tabarakullah became owner in possession to the extent of the whole of 2.40 acres of land. After sale of some land to one Islam, he was also recorded to be owner in possession of said land of plot No. 86. During MRR survey the land was recorded in MRR Khatian No. 279. Khatian No. 206/1 was recorded as MRR Khatian No. 289. Said Tabarakullah was also owner in possession of 35 decimals of land, 12 decimals of three plots and 23 decimals of plot No. 232. 

 4. Besides, after transfer of 73 decimals of land to said Islam and others, Tabarakullah was recorded to be owner in possession of 71 decimals, 39 decimals of three plots and 32 decimals of 15 plots along with the purchasers in MRR Khatian No.9. 

 5. By way of purchase, Tabarakullah was owner in possession of 54 decimals, 31 decimals of plot No. 177 and 23 decimals out of 46 decimals of plot No. 178 appertaining to khatian No. 23, which was recorded in MRR Khatian No. 21. Tabarakullah was thus owner in possession in said four khatians. 

 6. Tabarakullah died leaving two sons, namely, Mobarakullah and Shafiullah and two daughters, namely, Mahmuda Khatun and Fatema Khatun. By two deeds of gift being No. 4828 dated 30-6-73 and No. 6315 dated 9-10-73 Tabarakullah transferred in total 1.11 acres of land of MRR Khatian No. 199, 279, 23 and 21 to said two sons Shafiullah and Mobarakullah and delivered them possession. After such transfers he exhausted all his interest in said land. 

 8. Land of plot No. 232 of Khatian No. 199 was joint homestead land of plot No. 215 comprised of a pond. Other lands comprised of orchard and 'Nal' land. After marriage of said two daughters of Tabarakullah, Shafiullah and Mobarakullah jointly possessed and enjoyed the land without any partition by metes and bounds. 

 12. Their common case is that, the application was barred by principles of waiver, estoppel and acquiescence. Their further case was that respondent No. 7 exchanged 3 decimals of land of khatian No. 199 of mouza Aisapara and two decimals of land of khatian No. 23 of mouza Batagram in total 5 decimals of land by a deed of exchange being No. 8376 dated 10-7-96 with respondent No. 4 Fazlur Rahman in lieu of 5 decimals of land of khatian 40 of mouza Batagram and each of them got possession of his exchanged land. 

 21. There is no dispute that the preemptors and respondent No. 7 were in joint possession of the case land, which comprised of two mouzas of Aisapara and Batagram. By a sale deed dated 1-9-96 respondent No. 7 Mobarakullah transferred 55 decimals of Khatian No. 199 and 206(1) of mouza Aisapara and 20.5 decimals of khatian Nos. 23 and 13 of mouza Batagram in total 75.5 decimals of land to respondent No.4. And respondent Nos. 5 and 6 transferred 3.5 decimals of khatian Nos. 13 and 3 decimals of Khatian No. 23 of mouza Batagram and 5 decimals of khatian No. 199 of mouza Aisapara in total 11.05 decimals of land to respondent Nos. 1 to 3. 

 26. In cross-examination, he however, stated that he could not remember what land of which plot or which khatian he got by way of exchange. He could not remember the date of the deed of exchange. Who was the first-party and who was the second party in the exchange deed, he could not remember. He however, denied that the exchange deed was sham and that he did not get possession of the exchanged land. He could not remember who witnessed the exchange document. He further said that the exchange deed was not read over to him nor could he have read the deed. Lastly, he denied that the exchange was fake and/or sham, he had no knowledge. 

 28. In cross-examination, he stated that the exchanged land appertained to khatian No. 40 and was 200/250 chains away from the case land. Land of khatian No. 40 comprised of 5 plots belonged to nine persons. Every one of them was owner in possession in every plot. The land belonged to Muku Mia Muku Mia was his grandfather who died leaving three sons and one daughter. One son Abdur Rab who was his father married thrice. His mother was the first wife. Abdur Rab died leaving two wives, three sons and six daughters. He denied that his two step-mothers got 14 decimals out of 54 decimals of plot No. 22 of said khatian No. 40. At present said plot No. 22 was correctly recorded in their names. His step-brothers and sisters also got land by way of inheritance. 

 30. On calculation, it appears that Fazlur Rahman as one of three sons of Abdur Rab could have lawfully inherited at best 1.39 decimals of land out of entire 54 decimals of said plot No. 22 of khatian No. 40 left by his grandfather Muku Mia. So, he had no title/right to transfer 5 decimals of land by way of exchange.
